title: Durable agentProvider is written by the operator command and read through a store port
description:
SPIDR grandchild C of task-8e793ae3c63f41189bcc05f6d7c15605 (architect-2e480458, 2026-09-05). dependsOn grandchild B (set after B is filed) so the kind is already on the registry.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the durable store (copy the environment-store event-commit shape, without encryption — this value is not a secret), a closed refusal factory (AGENT_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN plus any store-layer codes), swapping B's fail-closed registry handler for the real one, composition of the store port. New files under apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/ or apps/daemon/src/settings/.

NOT IN SCOPE: RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS, MCP fence, spawn argv, pause bookkeeping, /sessions/read, UI.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.

Copy: apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-store.ts commitEnvironmentEvent; KNOWN_PROVIDERS at apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts:34.
definitionOfDone: A durable per-project `agentProvider` (claude|codex) with a per-goal override is written by `project.set_agent_provider` and read back. goalId "" is the project default; a non-empty goalId is the override. A read with no write returns the default `claude`. Assert the stored provider, not an in-memory field.

An unknown provider name is refused: assert code AGENT_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN AND its layer. The accepted names are taken from KNOWN_PROVIDERS (health-read.ts:34) — a test that mutates production to accept a third name without changing that roster goes RED.
The registry entry is the real store handler, not the fail-closed stub. A well-formed operator dispatch persists; a second read (new store instance against the same sqlite) returns what was written.
Gates quoted with `Test Files N passed`: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: REUSE KNOWN_PROVIDERS (health-read.ts:34). Import it. Do not declare a second list of provider names. Do not move the constant (that would touch health-read.ts, a concurrent-risk file).
Unknown provider refuses with a stable code AND layer (AGENT_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN). Valid names are exactly KNOWN_PROVIDERS.
Replace grandchild B's fail-closed handler; do not leave both. Unconfigured-daemon tests stay in B.
New production modules need a one-line .js bridge (copy environment-store.js). Target <=250 lines per production file; agent-spawner.ts is already 438 — do not grow it here.
FEATURES ONLY. No spawn, no /sessions/read, no UI, no MCP fence files.

Also note the shared checkout was dirty with 13 foreign paths at plan time. Peer dirt is never a stop condition: note it and continue. Never revert, stash, or `git add -A`.

RED TESTS FIRST — new apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-provider-store.test.ts. Write these arms and watch them FAIL before any production module exists. Copy the fixture shape from apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-test-fixtures.ts (openFileStore / openExistingStore / cleanUp) but do NOT import that file — it is the environment slice's test-tier scaffolding and hard-codes PROJECT_ID and a credential this slice has no use for. Open stores inline with `SqliteEventStore.openForProject(join(directory, "agent-provider.db"), PROJECT_ID)` from `@moe/store`, register them for cleanup, and close them in afterEach — a held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker on Windows.

Arms, each asserting a value, never mere truthiness:
  1. DEFAULT WITH NO WRITE. Read with goalId "" against a virgin store returns provider "claude". Assert the literal "claude" AND assert it equals KNOWN_PROVIDERS[0], so the derived default and the DoD's named default are pinned together.
  2. PROJECT DEFAULT ROUND-TRIPS. Write goalId "" provider "codex"; read goalId "" returns "codex".
  3. PER-GOAL OVERRIDE. With the project default at "codex", write goalId "goal-1" provider "claude"; read goalId "goal-1" returns "claude" AND read goalId "" still returns "codex" (the override does not overwrite the default). Read an UNWRITTEN goalId "goal-2" returns the project default "codex" — inheritance, not the hard-coded "claude".
  4. DURABILITY ACROSS INSTANCES (DoD item 3). Write through one store instance on a FILE path, close it, reopen the SAME path with a second `SqliteEventStore.openForProject(...)`, read through a store config built on the second instance, and assert the written provider comes back. This is the arm that proves the value is durable bytes and not an in-memory field — an ephemeral store cannot prove it, so this arm MUST be file-backed.
  5. UNKNOWN PROVIDER REFUSES (DoD item 2). Writing provider "gemini" returns a refusal whose `code` is exactly "AGENT_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN" AND whose `layer` is exactly the layer the closed map assigns it. Assert BOTH fields by literal equality. Also assert the refusal wrote NOTHING: `store.getAggregateVersion(<aggregateId>)` is unchanged across the refused call, and a subsequent read still answers the prior provider.

Probe the production write path over a candidate superset `[...KNOWN_PROVIDERS, "gemini", "llama", "", "CLAUDE"]`, collect the names it ACCEPTS into a Set, and assert set-equality with `new Set(KNOWN_PROVIDERS)`. This is the arm DoD item 2's mutation drill targets. Assert the swept candidate list is non-empty and strictly larger than KNOWN_PROVIDERS, so a sweep that silently yields zero cases cannot pass.

Every arm asserts against the production surface. Do not write a local helper that re-derives provider validity or default resolution — a property asserted against a reimplementation is vacuous.

THE CLOSED REFUSAL FACTORY — new apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-provider-contracts.ts plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./agent-provider-contracts.ts";` — copy apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-store.js verbatim in shape).   - `agentProviderRefusal(code)` — the ONLY way this slice mints a refusal. Takes the code alone and looks up the layer, so no call site can pair a code with the wrong layer.
  - `isKnownProvider(value: unknown): value is AgentProviderName` — the single validity predicate, implemented as a membership test against `KNOWN_PROVIDERS` IMPORTED from "../http/health-read.js". Import it; do NOT copy the names, do NOT declare a second list, and do NOT move the constant out of health-read.ts (that file is concurrent-risk and moving it is out of scope for this row). THE DURABLE STORE — new apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-provider-store.ts plus its one-line `.js` bridge. Copy the event-commit shape of `commitEnvironmentEvent` at apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-store.ts:91-115, WITHOUT the encryption: an agent provider name is a setting, not a secret, so there is no seal, no fingerprint and no credential source anywhere in this module.

Shape:
  - `AgentProviderStoreConfig` = { now: () => string; projectId: string; store: SqliteEventStore } — the environment config minus `credential`. `SqliteEventStore` is imported as a TYPE from "@moe/store". The dependency edge is already proven: apps/daemon/package.json:31 declares "@moe/store": "workspace:*", and apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-projection.ts:1 already imports this exact bare specifier and typechecks today. No manifest edit and no install is needed for this row.
  - `agentProviderAggregateId(projectId)` returning `agent-provider/${projectId}` — ONE aggregate per project holding the default and every per-goal override, with `goalId` carried in the event payload. Chosen over per-goal aggregates so a single fold answers both the default and any override, and so an override read can fall back to the default without a second aggregate read. Put that reasoning in a short module comment; it is the non-obvious call in this file.
  - `AGENT_PROVIDER_SET_EVENT = "moe.agent.provider.set"` declared HERE as an exact literal, matched by exact equality in the fold — never by a suffix rule (the environment fold documents why at environment-fold.ts:19-25).
  - `setAgentProvider(config, { commandId?, goalId, provider })`. Validation order is FIXED and documented: provider validity first via `isKnownProvider`, refusing `agentProviderRefusal("AGENT_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN")` and committing nothing. Each refusal is minted by exactly one surface so a doubly-invalid call has one stable answer. On success commit one event: aggregateId from the helper, `commandBytes` carrying the SUBJECT ONLY (kind, goalId, provider), `commandId: input.commandId ?? randomUUID()`, `committedAt: config.now()`, one event whose payload is the JSON-encoded { goalId, provider, updatedAt }, and `expectedVersion: config.store.getAggregateVersion(aggregateId)`.
  - `readAgentProvider(config, goalId)` folding `config.store.readEvents(aggregateId)` in order, later events winning, into a Map of goalId -> provider (a Map, NOT a bare object literal, so a `__proto__` or `constructor` goalId off the wire cannot be confused with a real entry). Resolution: the entry for a non-empty `goalId` if present, else the entry for "", else `DEFAULT_AGENT_PROVIDER`. A malformed or unparseable record is DROPPED rather than ignored, matching environment-fold.ts:12-16 — silently resurrecting a prior value is the more dangerous reading. A folded value that is not in KNOWN_PROVIDERS is also dropped, so a roster narrowed later cannot resurrect a name production no longer serves.

Do NOT translate a lost version race into a caller-shaped refusal: like the environment store, let the store's own ExpectedVersionConflictError propagate. The refusal roster here is CLOSED and every code in it is a fact about the CALLER's request; a lost race is a fact about the store. Say so in a comment. Keep this module under 250 lines; split before 400.

Run the step-2 arms now — they should go GREEN except any that depend on the command/registry swap.

SWAP B'S FAIL-CLOSED HANDLER AND COMPOSE THE STORE PORT. Rewrite the BODY of B's `runAgentProviderCommand` in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-provider-command.ts so the real store answers. Do not leave both handlers and do not add a second exported entry point — task rail 3 is explicit that the stub is REPLACED.

Task rail 3 says the unconfigured-daemon tests stay in B, so AGENT_PROVIDER_UNCONFIGURED must still be minted at B's layer when the store dependency is genuinely absent. COMPOSITION, in apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts. That file is already 449 lines — over the 400 split line — so add as FEW lines as the wiring allows and add no new logic there. `clock`, `projectId` and `store` are all already destructured in scope at line 157; the delegation pattern to copy is the `runPolicyWaiverDecideCommand({ ..., projectId, store })` call inside the handler closure at roughly line 264. Pass B's existing call site the store config `{ now: clock, projectId, store }` so the real path is reachable. If B's call site already passes an argument object, extend it; the ideal diff here is the added config only.

Now re-read what step 1 recorded about B's UNCONFIGURED test arm. If it is a UNIT arm calling the function directly with no store config, it stays green untouched and B's test file is NOT in your diff — prefer this outcome. If instead it dispatches through a fully-composed registry, it will now reach the real store and change answer; adjust THAT ARM ONLY, minimally, in place, so it still proves the unconfigured refusal at the seam that can still be unconfigured. If neither adjustment is honest — for instance if B pinned an unconditional refusal that the swap makes unreachable by design — stop and report rather than reshaping B's coverage on your own judgement.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
AGGREGATE SHAPE. Per-goal aggregates (agent-provider/<projectId>/<goalId>) were rejected: an override read must fall back to the project default, which would force a second aggregate read and a second version to reason about. ONE aggregate per project, with goalId carried in the event payload, lets a single fold answer the default, any override, and the inheritance rule together.

HOW THE UNCONFIGURED PATH SURVIVES THE SWAP. Task rail 3 says the fail-closed handler is REPLACED but the unconfigured-daemon tests STAY IN B. Those two only hold together if AGENT_PROVIDER_UNCONFIGURED is still mintable after the swap, so the real handler takes an OPTIONAL store config and keeps B's code and layer for the absent case. The alternative — deleting the unconfigured branch outright — would strand B's arms and force this row to edit coverage it does not own. Step 5 makes the worker read B's landed arm first, because whether B's test file is touched at all depends on whether that arm is a unit call or a composed-registry dispatch; the plan lists B's test path so this is not an out-of-plan discovery at step 5.

DEFAULT PROVIDER. Typing "claude" as a literal in this slice was rejected: health-read.ts already documents the ordering as deliberate, and a second literal is exactly how the two drift. Derived as KNOWN_PROVIDERS[0], with the test asserting both that it equals "claude" and that it equals KNOWN_PROVIDERS[0].

MODULE SPLIT. Contracts and store are separate files (the environment slice uses four: contracts/cipher/fold/projection). Two keeps each well under the 250-line target and keeps the closed refusal roster readable on its own. A single combined module was rejected only on that readability ground — it would still have fit.
